messages:
tom: Heads up — seeing steady KV cache memory growth on long-context runs when the runtime flips kernel selection to the 'tiled' path. Repro on our mixed A100/MI250 cluster (nvlink+pcie). Looks like page aliasing / alloc-hint mismatch rather than pure evict failure. :thinking:
sara: Can you paste the allocator trace and any page-table dumps you have? is eviction failing or are we just fragmenting into unusable holes?
tom: quick paste of an excerpt (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:02Z] alloc: gpu=GPU0 page_id=0x1a size=64kb alloc_hint=0x4 align=128 owner=runtime
[2026-03-15T09:12:02Z] kernel_expect: tiled stride=256 align=256
[2026-03-15T09:12:02Z] remap: page 0x1a -> 0x1a alias_detected=true owner->GPU1
[2026-03-15T09:12:02Z] evict: scanned=8 reclaimed=0 holes=3 fragmented=8192
[2026-03-15T09:12:02Z] kvcache: total_kv_pages=524k resident=512k free_holes=12 growth_bytes=+1.2GB/30m
```
cmd I ran: `./tools/kvtrace --pid 1234 --filter alloc,remap,evict --sample 60`
rajesh: That pattern screams shadowmap/aliasing edgecase. If the tiled kernel assumes 256B stride but allocator handed out 128B-aligned pages, compaction won't coalesce and alias checks miss because of different canonicalization rules. Have you tried forcing the non-tiled kernel?
tom: I forced `REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=tiled_noalign` and the growth persisted. When I forced the fallback scalar kernel (`REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=scalar`) the growth stops. Patching allocator to prefer 256 align for tiled path fixed a 1h run (no steady growth). So two hypotheses: (1) allocator alignment heuristic mismatch with kernel tiling, (2) page-table canonicalization differs between architectures so alias detection isn't symmetric on MI250 vs A100.
sara: Important: this only shows up under mixed-arch routing where requests hit both GPUs in a session and the KV entries get remapped across devices, right?
tom: yes — single-client longctx sessions that get routed across GPUs (burst+fallback) trigger it. It crops up when we do mid-session kernel switch (latency/cost policy).
rajesh: Short-term mitigation: add an allocator flag when selecting tiled kernel to force alignment >= stride. Also add an assert in the remap path: if alias_detected && (alloc_align < kernel_stride) then log and bump a metric. Long-term: unify page canonicalization rules across backends and ensure compaction code treats aliased ranges consistently. Also add a repro harness that does repeated cross-gpu remap under tiled selection.
tom: Opening PR with the allocator change + smoke test. Perf tradeoff looks <1% for our test set but we need broader perf runs. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5372 (WIP)
infra-bot: CI queued: kvcache-regressions/tiled-align-check #1423 (queued) :white_check_mark:
sara: Can you also add an alert on Console: kvcache.longctx.mem_growth_rate > 10% over 1h? This would have caught it earlier.
tom: yes will add metric and a short-run eval. Also saving trace in /artifacts/kvtrace/4299998766/ for postmortem.
rajesh: FYI I reproduced on MI250-only node but only after running a kernel selection toggle loop (force tiled->scalar->tiled) 100x. So it's both the alignment and the flip. Might be an ordering race in the page-table remap path.
sara: ok next steps: (1) land allocator alignment guard + test (tom), (2) add metric/alert (sara), (3) deeper backend canonicalization PR (rajesh). If anyone sees regressions after the allocator change ping here. :raised_hands:
tom: thanks — will update with CI + perf artifacts once the run finishes.
